newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance minister's wife ends TV show.
newsitem.headline: French finance minister's wife ends TV show.

text.p: Star television interviewer Anne Sinclair, the wife of France's new Socialist finance minister, will end her popular 13-year-old current affairs programme 7/7 next month, television channel TF1 said on Friday.
Sinclair will present the last of the hour-long Sunday evening prime time interviews of leading politicians on July 6, a week before her 49th birthday.

Prime Minister Lionel Jospin put her husband Dominique Strauss-Kahn in charge of a superministry of finance, economy and industry following the left-wing victory in a snap parliamentary election last Sunday.
"Early election, early decision," Sinclair said. A TF1 spokeswoman said Sinclair had planned to end the programme after the election which was originally scheduled next year.
Besides all leading French politicians, Sinclair has interviewed world leaders such as U.S. President Bill Clinton, German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and the late Israeli premier Yitzhak Rabin.

The pretty, dark-haired Sinclair had not interrupted her programme when Strauss-Kahn was industry minister in 1991-93. A prize-winning journalist, she will keep her job as deputy director of the private channel's news services.
